issues.legal_issue: Setting aside properties to fund religious worship does not transfer ownership to the religious beneficiaries when the governing decree places the properties in the residue and the setting aside provides only for worship expenses.
material_facts: A will bequeathed the estate to deities, but a court decree declared that bequest invalid and directed that provision be made for worship before the residue was divided among the heirs.
A commissioner recommended setting aside four properties to provide funds for worship and related religious occasions.
The final decree accepted the recommendation, and the properties were not physically partitioned between the heirs.
The taxpayer asserted that the properties had become dedicated property and that their income was therefore not assessable as his income.
issues.conclusion: The properties remained part of the residuary estate and were not dedicated to the deities; they were subject to an obligation to fund worship. The question was correctly answered against the taxpayer.
issues.legal_principle: The commissioner’s report must be read in the context of the governing decree. A direction to set aside properties or use their income to meet worship expenses does not, without an intention to transfer ownership, dedicate the properties to the religious beneficiaries. The decree’s terms placed the properties in the residue subject to the worship obligation. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on.

rule.if: income_tax_appeal_over_property_income and will_bequest_invalidated and decree_required_worship_funding_before_residue_distribution and report_identified_properties_as_funding_source and report_specified_annual_funding_without_expressly_transferring_title and properties_not_physically_partitioned

predicates.income_tax_appeal_over_property_income: The proceeding concerned the tax treatment of income from properties whose ownership was disputed.
predicates.will_bequest_invalidated: A court declared invalid a will’s bequest of the estate to religious beneficiaries.
predicates.decree_required_worship_funding_before_r: A court directed that provision be made for worship before the estate’s residue was distributed among heirs.
predicates.report_identified_properties_as_funding_: A commissioner recommended using identified properties as a source of funds for worship and related religious occasions.
predicates.report_specified_annual_funding_without_: The commissioner’s report specified annual amounts for religious expenses but did not expressly state that ownership of the properties was transferred.
predicates.properties_not_physically_partitioned: The properties had not been physically divided between the heirs.

issues.definition: When a property-income tax appeal concerns an invalidated bequest, a decree requires worship funding before distribution of the residue, and a report identifies properties as the funding source without expressly transferring title, the properties’ lack of physical partition does not prevent them from remaining in the residue subject to the worship obligation.
